page: Microsoft Azure F2s is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the FS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core, alongside 8 GB of local storage. This instance is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the F2s in the lower performance tiers across multiple metrics. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng register at 1037.99 and 2045.39 respectively, both falling within the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers reaching 14.46 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.46 GB/sec. Similarly, the Geekbench single-core score of 763.0 and multi-core score of 1386.0 reflect limited processing capabilities. Database operations and LLM inference for a small 135M model show slightly better but still weak performance, placing in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F2s offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources, though its low memory-to-vCPU ratio limits its utility for memory-intensive tasks. Given the poor benchmark results in compute, memory bandwidth, and database operations, this server is best suited for lightweight utility services, basic web serving, small-scale development testing, or simple background tasks that do not demand high throughput or rapid data processing.
